questions.question: The Char Dham pilgrimage circuit of Uttarakhand comprises Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and which other shrine?
questions.explanation: The four shrines of the Himalayan Char Dham in Uttarakhand are Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. Dwarka, Puri and Rameswaram belong to the separate pan-India Char Dham tradition propagated by Adi Shankaracharya.

questions.question: A shopkeeper mixes 26 kg of rice costing ₹45 per kg with 14 kg of rice costing ₹65 per kg. The cost price per kg of the mixture is:
questions.explanation: Total cost = 26 × 45 + 14 × 65 = 1170 + 910 = ₹2,080 for 40 kg, so the mixture costs 2080 ÷ 40 = ₹52 per kg.

questions.question: Find the next term of the series: 4, 10, 28, 82, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 3 and subtracting 2: 4×3−2 = 10, 10×3−2 = 28, 28×3−2 = 82, 82×3−2 = 244.

questions.question: Which country won the Thomas Cup 2024 in men's team badminton, defeating Indonesia 3–1 in the final at Chengdu?
questions.explanation: China regained the Thomas Cup in May 2024, beating Indonesia 3–1 in the final at Chengdu. India were the defending champions, having won the 2022 edition.

questions.question: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a row facing north. (i) Q sits at the extreme left. (ii) S sits immediately to the right of Q. (iii) P sits second from the right end. (iv) T sits immediately to the left of P. (v) R sits immediately to the right of S. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: Q takes seat 1 and S seat 2; R, immediately to the right of S, takes seat 3. P is second from the right end (seat 5) and T, immediately left of P, takes seat 4. The only remaining seat 6, the extreme right, goes to U. Final order: Q, S, R, T, P, U.

questions.question: In a school, three-fifths of the students are boys. If there are 40 girls, the total number of students in the school is:
questions.explanation: Girls form 1 − 3/5 = 2/5 of the total, so total = 40 × 5/2 = 100 students.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the molecular machines where amino acids are assembled into proteins. Mitochondria produce ATP, the Golgi apparatus packages proteins, and lysosomes carry out digestion of cellular waste.

questions.question: Which Indian state shares the longest international border with Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: West Bengal shares about 2,217 km of the roughly 4,096 km India–Bangladesh border — the longest stretch among the five bordering states (West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram).

questions.question: The sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic progression 7, 11, 15, … is:
Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanation: Rhombus, trapezium and rectangle are two-dimensional plane figures, while a cylinder is a three-dimensional solid.

questions.question: ISRO's Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory mission, was inserted into its planned halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point in:
questions.explanation: Launched on 2 September 2024, Aditya-L1 performed halo orbit insertion around the Sun–Earth L1 point on 6 January 2025, completing its 110-day cruise from Earth orbit.

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions. Statements: All phones are gadgets. Some gadgets are costly. Conclusions: I. Some phones are costly. II. All gadgets are phones. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: A) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
B) Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The costly gadgets may all be non-phone gadgets, so 'some phones are costly' is not certain. 'All gadgets are phones' wrongly reverses 'all phones are gadgets'. Hence neither conclusion follows.

questions.question: 3 pens and 4 pencils cost ₹51, while 5 pens and 2 pencils cost ₹57. The cost of one pen is:
questions.explanation: Subtracting the first equation from the second: 2 pens − 2 pencils = ₹6, so pen − pencil = 3. Substituting pen = pencil + 3 in 3p + 4q = 51 gives 7q = 42, q = 6 and p = 9. A pen costs ₹9.

questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy — bleeding gums, poor wound healing and anaemia — is caused by deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid), which is essential for collagen synthesis.

questions.question: The Konkan Railway, built along India's western coast, runs from Roha in Maharashtra to which major city in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Konkan Railway line runs from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangaluru in Karnataka, traversing the Konkan coast through Goa and parts of Karnataka.

questions.question: When a number is increased by 12.5%, it becomes 90. The number is:
questions.explanation: Increasing by 12.5% multiplies the number by 1.125 = 9/8. So the number = 90 × 8/9 = 80.

questions.question: Anil walks 8 m towards north from his house, then turns right and walks 9 m, and then turns left and walks 4 m. How far and in which direction is he from his house?
questions.explanation: Net displacement: north 8 m + north 4 m = 12 m, and 9 m east. Distance = √(12² + 9²) = √(144 + 81) = √225 = 15 m. Since the east component lies to the right of the north line, he is 15 m towards north-east of his house.

questions.question: The theme of the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting held at Davos in January 2025 was:
questions.explanation: The Davos 2025 meeting (20–24 January) was themed 'Collaboration for the Intelligent Age', focusing on AI and technological transformation. 'Rebuilding Trust' was the 2024 theme and 'Cooperation in a Fragmented World' the 2023 theme.

questions.question: If 1 March 2025 was a Saturday, then 1 April 2025 was a:
questions.explanation: March has 31 days, and 31 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 days ahead of Saturday gives Tuesday.

questions.question: A sum invested at compound interest amounts to ₹7,200 at the end of 4 years and ₹8,100 at the end of 5 years. The annual rate of interest is:
questions.explanation: The interest for the 5th year is earned on ₹7,200: 8100 − 7200 = 900. Rate = 900/7200 × 100 = 12.5% per annum.

questions.question: Myopia (short-sightedness), in which distant objects appear blurred, is corrected by using which type of lens?
questions.explanation: In myopia the eye's image of distant objects forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens pushes the image back onto the retina. Cylindrical lenses correct astigmatism, and convex/bifocal lenses address hypermetropia or presbyopia.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won a bronze in weightlifting (69 kg category) at the Sydney 2000 Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.

questions.question: Two equal vessels contain milk and water in the ratios 5 : 3 and 3 : 1 respectively. If both are emptied into a single container, the ratio of milk to water in the mixture is:
questions.explanation: Take each vessel as 1 unit. Milk = 5/8 + 3/4 = 5/8 + 6/8 = 11/8; water = 3/8 + 1/4 = 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8. Hence milk : water = 11 : 5.

questions.question: If PINK is coded as 1691411, where each letter is replaced by its position in the English alphabet written in order, then BLUE is coded as:
questions.explanation: B = 2, L = 12, U = 21, E = 5, and writing the positions one after another gives 2-12-21-5 → 212215. This matches PINK = 16-9-14-11 → 1691411.

questions.question: WAVES 2025, India's first global summit on the media and entertainment sector (World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit), was hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: WAVES 2025, positioned as a global media and entertainment summit on the lines of Davos, was held in Mumbai from 1–4 May 2025.

questions.question: The words Distant, Diverse, Divert and Divide are arranged as in an English dictionary. Which word comes third?
questions.explanation: Dictionary order: distant (dis…), then diverse and divert (both diver…, with 's' before 't' at the sixth letter), and finally divide (divi…, where 'i' comes after 'e'). So the third word is divert.

questions.question: Study the data: In a college of 800 students, the numbers opting for various streams are: Science 240, Commerce 320, Arts 160 and Vocational 80. Next year, Commerce enrolment is projected to rise by 15% while Arts enrolment falls by 10%. What is the net change (in number of students) across these two streams?
questions.explanation: Commerce rises by 15% of 320 = 48; Arts falls by 10% of 160 = 16. Net change = 48 − 16 = +32 students.

questions.question: Which pollutant in drinking water is responsible for methaemoglobinaemia, popularly known as 'blue baby syndrome'?
questions.explanation: Nitrates ingested by infants are converted to nitrites, which oxidise haemoglobin into methaemoglobin that cannot carry oxygen, giving the skin a bluish tinge. Excess fluoride causes fluorosis; arsenic and lead cause chronic poisoning.

questions.question: The Tungabhadra, on whose banks the ruins of Hampi stand, is a major tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra is formed by the Tunga and Bhadra rivers and flows east to join the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh. Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, stands on its banks.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. Working together with C, they finish the work in 5 days. C alone can complete the work in:
A person walks 8 km towards south, turns left and walks 6 km, turns left again and walks 8 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing south, his left is east: he moves 6 km east. The next left turn (facing east) takes him 8 km north, cancelling the 8 km south. The final right turn (facing north) moves him 4 km further east. Net displacement = 6 + 4 = 10 km towards east.

questions.question: UEFA Euro 2024, held in Germany, was won by Spain, which defeated ______ 2–1 in the final:
questions.explanation: Spain beat England 2–1 in the Euro 2024 final at Berlin on 14 July 2024, winning a record fourth European championship.

questions.question: Find the next letter of the series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
questions.explanation: Letter positions: B(2), D(4), G(7), K(11), P(16). The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: 16 + 6 = 22 = V.

questions.question: The average of five consecutive multiples of 7 is 42. The largest of these multiples is:
questions.explanation: For consecutive multiples, the average equals the middle (third) multiple: 42. The five multiples are 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, so the largest is 42 + 2 × 7 = 56.

questions.question: Concentrations of DDT keep rising at successively higher trophic levels in a food chain. This biomagnification occurs mainly because DDT is:
options: A) lipid-soluble and not readily metabolised or excreted, so it accumulates in the fatty tissues of predators
B) water-soluble and rapidly excreted from the bodies of animals
C) decomposed completely by sunlight before it can enter any organism
D) synthesised by producers as a natural by-product of photosynthesis
questions.explanation: DDT is highly lipid-soluble and resistant to metabolic breakdown, so organisms retain it in fatty tissue instead of excreting it. Predators therefore ingest the accumulated burden of all their prey, and concentration multiplies up the food chain.

questions.question: Disqualification of a legislator on the ground of defection is dealt with by which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, contains the anti-defection law. The Eighth Schedule lists official languages, the Ninth deals with land-referenced laws, and the Twelfth covers municipal bodies.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the speed of the stream is 2 km/h. The boat rows 36 km downstream and then returns to the starting point. The total time taken for the trip is:
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 12 km/h → 36/12 = 3 h. Upstream speed = 8 km/h → 36/8 = 4.5 h. Total = 3 + 4.5 = 7.5 hours.

questions.question: In the first row of a number pattern are 3, 7, 16 and in the second row are 6, 13, ?, the relation being the same in both rows. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: In each row, the second number is (2 × first) + 1 and the third number is (2 × second) + 2. Row 1: 2×3+1 = 7, 2×7+2 = 16. Row 2: 2×6+1 = 13, so ? = 2×13+2 = 28.

questions.question: As of February 2025, India ranks third in the world in the number of Ramsar wetland sites, with 89 designated sites. Which country tops the list?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom has the largest number of Ramsar sites in the world (about 175), followed by Mexico; India stood third with 89 sites as of February 2025 after adding fresh designations.

questions.question: A watch gains 5 minutes in every hour and is set right at 6 a.m. When the watch indicates 3 p.m. on the same day, the actual time is:
questions.explanation: The faulty watch shows 9 hours elapsed while the true elapsed time is x hours. Gaining 5 minutes per hour: x + 5x/60 = 9, so 13x/12 = 9 and x = 108/13 = 8 4/13 hours. Actual time = 6 a.m. + 8 4/13 hours = 18 6/13 minutes past 2 p.m.

questions.question: Alloy A contains 70% copper and alloy B contains 20% copper. A mixture of A and B weighing 25 kg contains 44% copper. The quantity of alloy B in the mixture is:
questions.explanation: Copper in mixture = 44% of 25 = 11 kg. Let A = a, B = 25 − a: 0.7a + 0.2(25 − a) = 11 → 0.5a = 6 → a = 12 kg. So B = 25 − 12 = 13 kg.

questions.question: In a cross between a heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) and a dwarf pea plant (tt), the phenotypic ratio of the offspring is:
questions.explanation: Tt produces gametes T and t; tt produces only t. Offspring are Tt (tall) and tt (dwarf) in equal proportions — a 1 : 1 phenotypic ratio, typical of a test cross.

questions.question: The Servants of India Society, set up in 1905 to train national missionaries for the service of the country, was founded by:
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train devoted workers for national service. Tilak, by contrast, founded the Deccan Education Society and opposed Gokhale's moderate methods.

questions.question: A man invests ₹12,000 in two parts, partly at 5% per annum and the rest at 8% per annum simple interest. If the total annual interest received is ₹810, the amount invested at 8% is:
The Abel Prize for 2025, among the highest honours in mathematics, was awarded to:
questions.explanation: Japanese mathematician Masaki Kashiwara won the 2025 Abel Prize for his foundational work in algebraic analysis and the theory of D-modules. Michel Talagrand was the 2024 laureate.

questions.question: In a class test: A scored more than B; C scored less than D; E scored more than A; F scored more than D but less than A; and B scored more than D. Who scored the third highest?
questions.explanation: Chaining the clues: E > A > F > B > D > C (B > D from the last clue, and C is the lowest). E is first, A second, so F is third highest.

questions.question: A sum of ₹21,700 is divided among X, Y and Z. X receives two-fifths of the total, and the remaining amount is divided between Y and Z in the ratio 3 : 4. Y's share is:
Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The current flowing through the 3 Ω resistor is:
questions.explanation: In a parallel connection each resistor gets the full 12 V. Current through the 3 Ω resistor = V/R = 12/3 = 4 A (through the 6 Ω resistor it is 2 A, and the total drawn from the battery is 6 A).

questions.question: A trader marks his goods 50% above the cost price and, after allowing a discount, still earns a profit of 20%. The percentage discount allowed is:
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. Marked price = 150 and, at 20% profit, selling price = 120. Discount = 150 − 120 = 30 on 150, i.e. 30/150 = 20%. (Check: 150 × 0.8 = 120 = 20% profit on CP.)

questions.question: Four engineers W, X, Y and Z are assigned to four projects — Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Delta — one engineer per project. (i) Z is assigned Alpha. (ii) W is not assigned Alpha or Delta. (iii) Y is not assigned Gamma. (iv) X is not assigned Gamma or Delta. Who is assigned Delta?
questions.explanation: Z takes Alpha. X can take only Beta (not Gamma or Delta), so X = Beta. W cannot take Delta, so W takes the only remaining project, Gamma. That leaves Delta for Y, which is consistent with Y not being on Gamma.
